info.name: Taskpilot Agent Service
info.description: Requests and example responses for the Flask agent service. Set baseUrl to the service URL. The /pipeline request is called by the backend but is not exposed by the current Docker entrypoint (app.py); it is only defined in main.py.

request.description: Required JSON fields: project_name (string), defination (string). The spelling defination is part of the current API. Returns the model-generated JSON object; normally it contains new_defination.

response.name: 200 - initialized definition

request.description: Required JSON field: defination (string). Returns key_features as an array of strings.

response.name: 200 - features identified

body.raw:
{
  "project_name": "Task Manager",
  "defination": "A responsive application for organizing projects and tasks, with user accounts, task assignment, and progress tracking.",
  "key_features": [
    "User authentication",
    "Project and task management",
    "Task assignment",
    "Progress tracking",
    "Responsive design"
  ]
}

request.description: The Flask route requires defination (string) and key_features (array of strings). The backend client also sends project_name, although this route does not use or require it. Returns doc_name, doc_desc, doc_body, use_case_diagram, and er_diagram.

response.name: 200 - documentation generated

request.description: The Flask route requires defination (string) and key_features (array). The request shown matches the backend client fields: project_name, employees (name, designation, skillset), defination, development_type, complexity, and key_features. The generator also reads optional description and timeline fields, which the current backend client does not send.

response.name: 200 - tasks generated

body.raw:
{
  "project_name": "Task Manager",

}

request.description: This matches the payload constructed by backend/src/services/project.service.ts. The backend calls POST /pipeline, but the Dockerfile starts app.py, which does not define /pipeline; this request currently returns 404 against the deployed service. main.py defines the route and responds with name, description, doc_body, tasks, er_diagram, and use_case_diagram. That route reads definition (not description) for diagrams, while the backend currently sends description.
